newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks up on overseas gains, rate hope.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks up on overseas gains, rate hope.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 93.515 -0.065 Gold NY 324.25 Lon fix 321.95
*Stocks end 0.55 pct up on rate cut hopes, overseas gains. Turnover affected by options exercises. Volume 366 million, value A$1.352 bln, 1,064 stocks traded, 259 steady, 440 up, 325 down.
The Australian share market ended 0.55 pct higher on Friday, supported by overseas gains and general expectations of an official interest rate cut in the next few weeks.
The All Ordinaries index rose 14.8 points to 2,691.2, while the September share price index futures contract gained 19 points to 2,714, a 22.8 point premium to the underlying index.

There was some initial disappointment as the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) failed to deliver a rate cut this morning, but investors soon turned their hopes to the RBA's next meeting on August 5. "Everybody expects a cut then," one dealer said.
Dealers said the underlying sentiment remained firm, and that share prices were likely to continue higher next week.
"There is a lot of money coming in from overseas. Our market is seen to be cheap by comparison," Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan in Melbourne said.
Turnover amounted to A$1.35 billion, boosted by July series options exercises after Thursday's expiry. About half, or A$725 million was handled before market hours.
The banking sector received a lot of attention, but performances were mixed and the index only gained a moderate 0.35 percent.

Among others, Helix Resources sagged further, losing eight cents to 76 cents with brokers saying the low grades at its Gawler Craton prospects made Helix shares unattractive in light of the slide of the bullion price.

In other markets, Australian bond yields ended higher as the market booked profits and squared up after this week's strong rally, unable to push on the move in the absence of a monetary policy easing.
By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.52 percent, compared to Thursday's 6.44 percent.

The Australian dollar staged a short covering bounce Friday as another day passed with no rate cut, but most felt the fateful event had merely been postponed. By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), the dollar had settled at US$0.7398/03 having climbed from an early US$0.7361/66 and US$0.7348/53 late here Thursday.
